title: Simit Sesame Ring Bread

seo.imageCaption: Enjoy the taste of Istanbul with this easy recipe for authentic Turkish Simit, a delicious sesame-crusted ring bread perfect for breakfast or a snack!

description: Simit is Turkey's beloved sesame-crusted bread ring, a staple of Turkish breakfasts and street food culture. Its distinct chewy interior and crunchy, nutty exterior make it an irresistible treat. Perfect with cheese, olives, or a cup of Turkish tea, Simit brings the authentic taste of Istanbul right to your home.

instructions.title: Activate Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 1.5 cups warm water, 1 tablespoon granulated sugar, and 1 tablespoon active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active and ready.

instructions.title: Prepare Dough
instructions.text: Add 4 cups all-purpose flour and 1 teaspoon salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a sturdy spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn it out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Place the kneaded dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turning it once to coat all sides. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm, draft-free place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until the dough has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape Simit Rings
instructions.text: Gently punch down the risen dough to release the air. Divide the dough into 8-10 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope, about 18-20 inches (45-50 cm) long. Fold the rope in half lengthwise, twist the two strands together tightly, and then form a ring, pinching the ends firmly to seal them together.

instructions.title: Pekmez Dip and Sesame Coat
instructions.text: In a shallow dish, whisk together 1/2 cup grape molasses (pekmez) and 1/2 cup water until well combined. In another shallow dish, spread out the 2 cups of toasted sesame seeds. Dip each simit ring into the pekmez mixture, ensuring it is fully coated, then immediately transfer to the sesame seeds, pressing gently to adhere the seeds all over both sides of the ring.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Bake
instructions.text: Place the coated simit rings on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between them. Let them rest for another 15-20 minutes while you preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the simit are golden brown and cooked through.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the freshly baked simit from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Simit is traditionally best enjoyed warm, straight from the oven, typically served with Turkish cheese, olives, fresh tomatoes, and a steaming cup of Turkish tea.

tips: For a truly authentic texture, ensure your dough is kneaded sufficiently until it is very smooth and elastic. This develops the gluten, giving simit its characteristic chewiness.

If you cannot find grape molasses (pekmez), a good quality date molasses can be a substitute, though the flavor profile will be slightly different. It's crucial for the deep color and stickiness that holds the sesame seeds.
Simit is best eaten fresh on the day it's baked. If you have leftovers, lightly toast them in a dry pan or oven to regain some of their crispness before serving.
